figures.finding: A Croatian resident pays income tax at two rates set each year by the municipality or city of residence: a lower rate (15% up to 20–23% by size of place) on annual income up to €60,000 and a higher rate (25% up to 30–33%) above; 20% and 30% apply where the place sets none; each person has a personal allowance of €600 a month.
figures.applies: 2026. Each place decides its two rates by 30 November for the next year; the rate of each place was not gathered here. The rates of all 556 towns and municipalities, as in force on 1 November 2026, are taken from the Tax Administration's full table; each place's decision is published in Narodne novine by the end of November and applies from 1 January.

sources.said: Annual tax brackets (EUR) Tax rate (%) Over Not over 0 60,000 15 to 23 60,000 25 to 33

A municipality can choose a lower rate in the range from 15% to 20% and a higher rate in the range from 25% to 30%. A town can choose a lower rate in the range from 15% to 21% and a higher rate in the range from 25% to 31%. A city and a county seat can choose a lower rate in the range from 15% to 22% and a higher rate in the range from 25% to 32%. The City of Zagreb can choose a lower rate in the range from 15% to 23% and a higher rate in the range from 25% to 33%.
Those locations for which a local self-government unit does not make a choice by the set deadline are subject to progressive tax rates of 20% and 30%.
Each individual is entitled to a personal allowance of EUR 600 per month.

figures.finding: An employee pays 20% pension contributions (15% first pillar, 5% second) on gross pay up to €11,958 a month (base reduced on pay up to €1,300), and the employer 16.5% health insurance on uncapped gross pay; other income (such as a fee) bears 10% from the income and 7.5% on top.

sources.said: Employee's social security contributions are pension contributions levied at the rate of 20% (15% first pillar payments, 5% second pillar payments).
EUR 11,958.00 monthly cap (applicable for both first and second pillar payments in case of salary).
Health insurance: 16.5% The basis for payment of employer’s social security contributions is gross salary, which is not capped.
Normally, other income is subject to social security contributions from received income, levied at 10%, and on top of income, levied at 7.5%.

figures.finding: The employer withholds tax monthly at the place's lower rate on pay up to €5,000 a month and the higher rate above; tax on other income (fees, royalties) is withheld by the payer at the lower rate without personal allowances.

sources.said: Monthly tax brackets (EUR) Tax rate (%) Over Not over 0 5,000 15 to 23 5,000 25 to 33

Tax levied on other income is withheld by a payer of income at the lower tax rate (ranging between 15% and 23%, depending on the individual's place of residence or habitual abode in Croatia) without provision for taxpayers to claim personal allowances.

figures.finding: A fee paid to a foreign entity for a non-resident artist's or entertainer's performance in Croatia bears 10% withholding, and then the performer owes no personal income tax or contributions; a non-resident paid directly is taxed on the fee as other income, with an extra 30% expense allowance.

sources.said: Fees paid to foreign enterprises by domestic or foreign payers for the performance of nonresident artists, entertainers, and sportspersons in Croatia are subject to a 10% withholding tax

Non-resident performers (artists, entertainers, athletes) are not required to pay PIT if the fee for their performance is paid to a foreign legal entity and subject to withholding tax (WHT) in line with corporate income tax (CIT) legislation.
The income of non-residents arising from artistic, entertainment, sport, literary and visual art-related activities, and the activities connected with the press, radio, and television shows.

figures.finding: Copyright royalties are taxed as other income with an extra 30% of the income allowed as expenditure; for a delivered work of art a further 25% is non-taxable (55% in all).

sources.said: Additional expenditures shall be recognised in the amount of 30% of the income acquired on the basis of: Royalties paid pursuant to a special act governing copyright and related rights
in case of royalties received for the delivered work of art, 25% of the amount is considered non-taxable, i.e. total income is decreased by 55% (30% + 25%).

figures.finding: VAT is 25%; a resident must register when the annual value of transactions exceeds €60,000.

sources.said: The general VAT rate is 25%.
Registration for VAT purposes by a resident is mandatory where the annual value of transactions exceeds EUR 60,000.

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; the self-employed file by the end of February of the next year, while for employees the Tax Administration makes the annual assessment; tax assessed is due within 15 days of the assessment.

sources.said: The tax year is the calendar year.
The annual tax return filing deadline is the end of February of the current year for the previous year.
